correctness.rationale: Thin SVD yields signed coefficients mean*(1-alpha±r). Their absolute values give the exact contrast map T_c(r): r/c below c, c/r above c, with rank loss exactly at c. Transform x=log(r)/log(c); integer exponents hit rank one in exactly k steps, nonintegers enter (c,1) after floor(x) steps and undergo contrast involution. Tracking the polar signs for both alpha<1 and alpha>1 proves E_{t+2}=(1-alpha)E_t, not merely a singular-value relation. Equal singular, rank-one and zero starts are separately handled. Exact rational and 300 numerical random-frame checks passed; the proof establishes all quantifiers.

value.rationale: For the natural complete two-row isotropic slice at every stable off-line-search fixed step, this gives a nontrivial full phase portrait: generic finite-time entry into a scalar two-step orbit versus discrete exact finite-time rank-loss resonances, plus explicit subsequent rates. The source leaves non-line-search trajectory shape undetermined despite its general fixed-step formula. The result explains how step choice and exact initial spectrum jointly control algorithmic rank and contraction, rather than supplying a small parameter gain.
